name: dislocker
summary: Read BitLocker encrypted volumes under Linux.
highlights: -c — decrypt volume using a clear key (default)
-f — decrypt volume using the bek file (on USB key)
-k — decrypt volume using the FVEK directly
-K — decrypt volume using the VMK directly
-l — put messages into this file (stdout by default)
-O — BitLocker partition offset, in bytes (default is 0)
-p — decrypt volume using the recovery password method
usage: dislocker [-hqrsv] [-l LOG_FILE] [-O OFFSET] [-V VOLUME DECRYPTMETHOD -F[N]] [-- ARGS...]

flags.name: --clearkey
flags.description: decrypt volume using a clear key (default)

flags.name: --bekfile
flags.description: decrypt volume using the bek file (on USB key)

flags.name: --fvek
flags.description: decrypt volume using the FVEK directly

flags.name: --vmk
flags.description: decrypt volume using the VMK directly

flags.name: --logfile
flags.description: put messages into this file (stdout by default)

flags.name: --offset
flags.description: BitLocker partition offset, in bytes (default is 0)

flags.name: --recovery-password
flags.description: decrypt volume using the recovery password method

flags.name: --readonly
flags.description: do not allow one to write on the BitLocker volume

flags.name: --stateok
flags.description: do not check the volume's state, assume it's ok to mount it

flags.name: --user-password
flags.description: decrypt volume using the user password method

flags.name: --verbosity
flags.description: increase verbosity (CRITICAL errors are displayed by default)

flags.name: --volume
flags.description: volume to get metadata and keys from
